limitations: In-sample nuisance orthogonality is algebraically guaranteed and cannot establish generalisation.
Calibration examples and candidates have been previously inspected; OOF nuisance checks do not make them fresh.
Removing a linear mean-effect span does not remove all nonlinear or item-specific nuisance information.
No content direction is removed. Evaluation-versus-content remains unresolved.
Raw projected and unit-normalized outputs are both retained; no sign flip, layer search, or favourable candidate selection.
Raw score levels and cross-fold pooled AUROC are not claimed calibrated or comparable.
